label: The 310-byte residual after AGENTS.md:181 is the delivery tail, not headroom: an insertion of N bytes evicts N bytes of already-delivered rules on the 16,384-byte carrier. A 284-293 B insertion leaves :182 as a 17-18 byte fragment and removes :183 entirely.

Eviction brackets for an insertion after AGENTS.md:181: at most 27 B evicts nothing live; 28-168 B evicts :183 (140 B); 169-310 B evicts :183 and :182. The planned 283 B draft (284 with newline) sits in the worst bracket; a shape-only 154 B draft sits in the middle one.

Iteration 9's '17 B to spare' is evidence of eviction, not slack: 16,384 - 16,074 - 293 = 17 B is the delivered prefix of :182. The size measurements of the card and template targets are unaffected because neither file is size-bounded.

The only zero-eviction placement is the region already outside the cut: AGENTS.md:186 starts at byte 16,888, so extending the existing 'Plan before acting' line costs nothing on the truncating carrier and is delivered in full on the six runtimes without a per-file budget.

No independent carrier restates the two clauses the insertion would evict: a tree-wide phrase search returns only copies of AGENTS.md (barter overlay backups, a repin backup set, a doctor output snapshot) and nothing under .skilled/repo-rules.

The authoring card is intent-gated, not operator-gated: ROUTER.md:39 lists it in the IMPLEMENT resource map, orchestrate.md:465 rejects a spec-folder write without a prior card Read, and commands/speckit/implement.md:92 states that the writing session follows it. A dispatched child with no user present therefore reaches the card whenever the intent routes.

Final ranked recommendation: amend seven lines across three existing files - card :113, :120, :123, :124; template :124, :126; AGENTS.md :186. Ranked carriers: amended card+template lines > amended existing AGENTS.md line at :186 > inserted AGENTS.md bullet after :181 > hook injection > validator backstop > session-invokes-command. No new file, hook, command, rule, or bullet.

AGENTS.md is 27,372 B against the 16,384-byte per-file limit, so 10,988 B (40.1%) never reaches that carrier, including 'Settled stays settled', 'Plan before acting', 'Do not stop early' and 'Do not ask permission to continue an already-approved, in-scope step'. No other runtime in the tree documents a per-file rule budget.
On a file delivered under a documented size bound, an insertion of N bytes displaces N bytes of already-delivered text; residual bytes past the cut are live instruction, never capacity.
The recommendation may not buy arrival on one carrier by removing existing rules from that same carrier.

direction: Price an insertion into a size-bounded rule file by residual bytes.
reason: The metric treats live instruction as spare capacity and inverts the sign of the cost.
